Thanks Neha — that sounds great. A few clarifying points from my side so legal/procurement know the ask: 

- MedTech processes patient-derived signals; we require clear commitments on PII handling. Our default preference is that vendors act as processor for customer-provided data.
- We need an explicit list of subprocessors (cloud provider + any inference/ops partners) and a process for notifying us of changes.
- Breach notice: procurement prefers a 72-hour notification SLA. If you cannot commit to a hard SLA, please provide the typical notice timeline and escalation path.
- Data residency: all model inference involving EU patient data must be processed in an EU region. Is Redwood able to pin EU-only processing for our account?
- Retention: we'd like options to cap input retention (e.g., default 30 days) and longer-term storage only if we opt in.

Hi all — thanks for the clear list, Julia. Below is a short, shareable summary you can use in your procurement review. I’ve also attached a one-page DPA summary.

1) Roles (controller vs processor)
- For the purposes of the DPA: MedTech Solutions will be the Controller for any personal data you supply for inference. Redwood Inference will act as Processor for those inputs and only process them per your documented instructions and the DPA. Redwood may act as Controller for limited operational telemetry and aggregated, de-identified metrics related to service health; those do not include customer PII.

2) Subprocessors
- Current subprocessors: Amazon Web Services (AWS) — primary hosting (us-east-1, eu-west-1), Google Cloud Platform (GCP) — backup and select EU regions (europe-west1), and FastServe Inc. — managed inference orchestration.
- We maintain an up-to-date public list at: https://www.redwood.com/legal/subprocessors
- Change process: Redwood notifies customers 30 days prior to adding a new subprocessor and provides a chance to review the new subprocessor.

3) Breach notification
- Commitment: Redwood will notify customers without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of confirming a breach affecting customer data. Notification will include incident details, scope of data affected, mitigation steps, and recommended customer actions.

4) Data residency & EU-only processing
- Hosted: We offer model routing to EU regions and can pin EU-only processing for accounts under Dedicated or Private deployments. For strict EU-only residency with contractual guarantees, we typically recommend Redwood Dedicated or a Private deployment (VPC) to meet regulatory controls.

5) Retention policies
- Default behavior (hosted): input payloads used for inference are retained for 30 days for troubleshooting and quality monitoring by default; logs/telemetry are retained for 90 days.
- Options: Customers may request shorter or zero retention for inputs via contractual terms or select Dedicated/Private deployments where retention controls are configurable.

Attachments: redwood_dpa_summary.pdf (one-page summary); I also placed an export of the subprocessors list on the secure drive link below.

Related links:
- Subprocessors page: https://www.redwood.com/legal/subprocessors
- Export (S3 link, shared with Julia): https://redwood-storage.example.com/exports/MT-2026-0042/subprocessors.csv

Next steps for procurement: If a hard 72-hour SLA is required as an unconditional contractual penalty, let us know — we can escalate to commercial for review. Otherwise, the middle-ground language above is standard and accepted by most of our enterprise customers.
